title: Shop/update fires about once a minute with only updated_at changed — what triggers it?
text: Hi everyone, This looks related to Store is spamming shop_update webhook, anyway to stop? , but we’ve narrowed it down a bit further, so I’m starting a new thread. What we see On a public app subscribed to shop/update (app-scoped via shopify.app.toml , API version 2026-07, delivered through Google Pub/Sub), a few stores send shop/update about once a minute, around the clock. The busiest one sent about 42,000 in 30 days. These aren’t retries or duplicate subscriptions: Nearly every delivery has its own X-Shopify-Webhook-Id and X-Shopify-Event-Id . X-Shopify-Triggered-At is within a minute of when we receive it. We compared consecutive payloads from one of these stores. Across 9 deliveries, the only field that changed was updated_at . Every other field in the payload was identical. Our app doesn’t write to the Shop on these deliveries. Our handler only reads the Shop. Questions What kinds of changes cause shop/update to fire when no field in the payload changes except updated_at ? For example, does writing a shop-owned metafield (by another app, via metafieldsSet ) bump the Shop’s updated_at and fire shop/update ? Are there other Shop-level writes not visible in the payload that do the same? If we set include_fields without updated_at , how long is the window in which identical payloads are debounced? Would deliveries about a minute apart be dropped? Is there a supported way to get shop/update only when specific fields change (for example plan_name )? Events doesn’t seem to support a Shop topic yet. Thanks! 3 posts - 3 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Developer needs a way to stop excessive shop/update webhooks.

title: Explorer: Reliable Read-After-Write Verification for Native Glide Users Table Webhook Workflows?
text: Hello Glide Community! We’re developing Monster AI Languages on Glide’s Explorer plan, using native Glide Tables. Our application’s Users table is also its User Profiles table, so migrating that table to Big Tables is not an appropriate solution. We have an existing server-side webhook-triggered workflow that: 1. Receives an HTTPS POST from our Google Cloud Run service. 2. Extracts a specific User_Row_ID and three administrative field values using Query JSON. 3. Queries the native Users table for the exact User_Row_ID. 4. Executes Set Column Values against the matching Users row. This generally works, but we need to reliably verify that all three values were actually persisted to the intended Users row, rather than simply treating HTTP webhook acceptance as proof of success. Our technical questions 1. Sequential Query consistency If a webhook workflow executes: Query → Set Column Values → Query Does the second Query retrieve freshly persisted values, or might it reuse cached or previously evaluated results? 2. Write completion guarantees Does Set Column Values complete its database persistence before the next server-side workflow action executes? 3. Independent verification workflow Could we use a separate webhook-triggered, read-only workflow that queries the same Users row after the original write workflow has executed? Would this second execution retrieve independently evaluated, current stored values? Are there known consistency delays? 4. Returning actual stored values Could the second workflow use Trigger Webhook to send its Query results to our Cloud Run HTTPS endpoint, allowing our JavaScript to compare the returned Row ID and three actual stored values against the expected values? 5. Explorer-compatible production architecture Glide’s AI support agent, Fin, advised that webhook-triggered workflows with non-Big Table sources may not provide reliable real-time read/write behavior, and that Big Tables are recommended for synchronous saves. However, our Users table must remain the application’s native User Profiles table. What is Glide’s recommended, supported mechanism for verifying successful updates to a native Users/User Profiles table on Explorer? We are not seeking access to the external Glide Data API or an expensive plan upgrade. We already use Google Cloud Run, Firestore, and Stripe for secure subscription administration. We want a reliable acknowledgment or reconciliation mechanism without introducing unnecessary architectural complexity. If possible, we’d particularly appreciate clarification from a Glide staff member or engineer regarding the actual persistence and Query consistency guarantees. Thank you for your guidance! John Mastronardo Developer, Monster AI Languages Glide Explorer Plan If a Glide staff member needs additional account or application details, I would be happy to provide them privately. 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic
triage_reason: Developer needs reliable read-after-write verification for native Glide webhooks.

title: Feature Request – Allow replacing an auto-translated language when the Translate & Adapt limit is reached
text: Title: Feature Request – Allow replacing an auto-translated language when the Translate & Adapt limit is reached EnglishHello Shopify Team and Community, I would like to suggest an improvement to Shopify Translate & Adapt regarding the automatic translation language limit. Currently, stores located in France can automatically translate up to 8 languages. However, once this limit has been reached, removing a previously translated language does not free up a slot to translate another language. This creates an unnecessary restriction for international merchants. Example: A merchant has used all 8 automatic translation slots. One of those languages is no longer commercially relevant, and the merchant wants to replace it with another language to target a new market. Even after deleting the unused language, the merchant cannot automatically translate the new one. My suggestion: Shopify should allow merchants to permanently remove an automatically translated language and reuse the freed slot for another language. We are not asking for unlimited automatic translations, but for the flexibility to manage the languages according to evolving business needs. Questions for Shopify: Is there currently an official way to replace a previously auto-translated language? Could Shopify introduce a feature to release and reassign translation slots? Is this improvement being considered for Translate & Adapt? I believe this would be particularly valuable for merchants expanding into different international markets. Thank you for your feedback. Bonjour à l’équipe Shopify et à la communauté, Je souhaite proposer une amélioration de Shopify Translate & Adapt concernant la limite du nombre de langues traduites automatiquement. Actuellement, les boutiques situées en France peuvent traduire automatiquement jusqu’à 8 langues. Cependant, lorsque cette limite est atteinte, supprimer une langue déjà traduite ne permet pas de libérer une place pour en traduire une autre. Cette restriction pose un problème pour les commerçants internationaux. Exemple : Un commerçant a utilisé ses 8 possibilités de traduction automatique. Une langue ne présente plus d’intérêt commercial et il souhaite la remplacer par une autre pour développer un nouveau marché. Même après avoir supprimé l’ancienne langue, il ne peut pas traduire automatiquement la nouvelle. Ma proposition : Permettre aux commerçants de supprimer définitivement une langue traduite automatiquement et de réutiliser l’emplacement libéré pour une nouvelle langue. Il ne s’agit pas de demander un nombre illimité de traductions gratuites, mais simplement de pouvoir adapter les langues de sa boutique à l’évolution de son activité. Mes questions à Shopify : Existe-t-il actuellement une procédure officielle pour remplacer une langue traduite automatiquement ? Shopify pourrait-il ajouter une fonctionnalité permettant de libérer et réattribuer les emplacements de traduction ? Cette évolution est-elle envisagée pour Translate & Adapt ? Cette amélioration serait particulièrement intéressante pour les commerçants qui développent leurs ventes à l’international. Merci pour vos retours. 2 posts - 1 participant Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant requesting a feature to replace auto-translated languages when limits are reached.
